comment: Source of truth for the MIDI-first score of the whole run (openspec/changes/adaptive-soundtrack design §3, §4, §11, §12). tools/score/score_gen.lua composes every section listed here into web/audio/score/<song>/<section>.mid and packs this map into web/audio/score/score.json (for demon-score.js) and lib/game/song_map.dart (for SongDirector). Edit this file, then rerun the generator; never edit the outputs. There is no recorded music any more: every scene of the game plays a song of this map. Section kinds: loop (repeats until a move), tail (plays once; then its `hold` bars repeat, or it hands over to `next`), bridge (plays once and always hands over to `next` at its end). `next` names a section of the same song, or `song:section` of another song (a bridge into the next song's grid). `mask: all` plays every track except the fleet layer; otherwise the tier masks apply (`masks` on the song or section override the shared ones; a string names a set of `maskSets`). `hatch` numbers the carrier's hatch sections, `wave` orders a sector's wave-progress sections, `bonus` names the bonus level a section plays (bonus-levels: `stormfront`). `fx: worldized` passes the section through the band-pass small-room chain of design §4.4. Grids are integer samples per 4/4 bar at 48 kHz (tools/music_motifs.py BAR_SAMPLES).

bridges.comment: Which bridge song plays between two songs (`from>to`; `c` is any carrier). It plays at the source song's tempo from the end of the source's written tail (the clear or the victory) and hands over to the destination's arrival on its last bar line. Pivots from art/music/campaign.json `bridges` and design §3.1.

cackle.character: the cackle: a falling chromatic laugh on lead and choir over an organ cluster and timpani

alienwin.character: the twisted triumphant march in E Phrygian dominant

stingers.comment: Accents in the current key: `deg` is a scale degree of the playing section's key (1-7, may exceed 7), `semi` a chromatic step from its tonic, `oct` the MIDI octave (C4 = 60), `drum` a GM drum note. `t` and `len` are in beats from the anchor, the next multiple of `quantum` beats on the score's grid (with negative `t` the stinger leads into its anchor). `spacing` is the minimum beats between two of one stinger.
